title: Project 2025 Proposals on Presidential Control and Civil-Rights Enforcement
description_short: Project 2025 proposed greater presidential control and changes to federal civil-rights enforcement, remedies, data collection, immigration, reproductive rights, and surveillance.
description_medium: The Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights’ Project 2025 overview says the blueprint would increase presidential control and change federal civil-rights enforcement. It highlights proposed limits on administrative remedies and disparate-impact enforcement, cuts to civil-rights data collection, and changes to immigration, reproductive-rights, and surveillance policy. These are projected consequences of proposals, not proof that all freedoms have been eliminated.
description_long: The Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights’ Project 2025 overview describes a blueprint that would increase presidential control and change federal civil-rights enforcement. It highlights proposals to limit administrative remedies and disparate-impact enforcement, reduce civil-rights data collection, and change immigration, reproductive-rights, and surveillance policy. These are projected consequences of proposals, rather than a record of completed actions. The supplied packet does not identify a specific policy as implemented or document effects on a particular right. It therefore supports describing the blueprint’s proposed direction and the overview’s projected policy changes, but not saying that all freedoms or constitutional protections have been eliminated. The account also does not establish that every proposal took effect, or specify what effects any individual proposal produced. This entry is limited to the proposal areas named in the overview: federal civil-rights enforcement, administrative remedies, disparate-impact enforcement, data collection, immigration, reproductive rights, and surveillance. It does not attribute implementation or realized outcomes to Donald Trump.
